indicator_definition: This indicator measures the proportion of women among members of boards of directors of the largest publicly listed companies, expressed as a percentage of all board members. It covers both executive and non-executive board members. Data are collected by Eurostat in cooperation with the European Institute for Gender Equality (EIGE).
rationale: Women remain underrepresented in senior decision-making positions in the corporate sector. Increasing the share of women on company boards promotes gender equality and is associated with better governance and business performance. Progress means a sustained increase in the proportion of women in board-level positions.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected from national sources by Eurostat in cooperation with EIGE. The indicator covers the largest publicly listed companies registered in each country, specifically those listed on each country's main national stock exchange. Board members include both supervisory and management board members.
indicator_name: Women on boards of large listed companies
